concepts.def: Pollution from a single identifiable location (factory pipe, oil spill).
Diffuse pollution from many sources (urban run-off, agricultural fertiliser).
Released directly into the environment, e.g., SO2 from coal combustion.
Formed by reaction of primary pollutants, e.g., tropospheric ozone, sulfuric acid.
Toxic compounds resistant to degradation, e.g., DDT, PCBs; covered by Stockholm Convention (2001).
PM10 and PM2.5: airborne particles linked to respiratory and cardiovascular disease.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Pollution — a core area of A-Level Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Pollution brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Pollution.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
